long_biography.plain_text:
Licensing connected Andrea Camerana's early Armani career to the fashion house's international partners. After joining the group from Danone in 2000, he became vice-president of marketing and licensing, overseeing arrangements that included Emporio Armani watches and jewellery. He also served as an independent director of Fossil, one of the group's licensees.

Sustainability became Camerana's next corporate responsibility, placing environmental and social policy nearer the company's senior management. His remit included the Armani/Values platform and work on regenerative materials across the fashion supply chain. Following Giorgio Armani's death, he remained on the company board and joined the Giorgio Armani Foundation board, contributing to governance of the founder's succession framework.
